purpose: Reference-led dissection for a gothic stone post-panel-post guard asset before generating the next tool plan.

reference.title: Historic Gothic Architectural Stone Balcony
reference.author: Konrad's Photo
reference.license_or_access_note: Pexels public page; use here is limited to morphology reference and workflow discussion, not texture or mesh copying.

components.observed_reference_shape: Left square stone pier with vertical mass, side shadow, and carved face zones.

candidate_blender_tools.use: Create stacked pier body blocks and broad cap/base slabs.
Soften pier edges after block assembly.
Keep pier, trim, and shadow recess material roles distinct.

components.observed_reference_shape: Right square stone pier matching the left pier, used to prove symmetry and modular spacing.

candidate_blender_tools.use: Build one pier from block parts.
Mirror repeated pier-side trim when the source declares symmetry.
Match softened stone block edges.

components.observed_reference_shape: Tall pointed-arch recesses inset into the pier faces, with raised border trim.

candidate_blender_tools.use: Define the pointed arch curve/profile before cutter creation.
Convert sampled arch profile points into a deterministic cutter or raised trim mesh.
Cut a shallow arch recess into a pier face.
Bevel the arch trim and recess rim.

components.observed_reference_shape: Heavy square cap slabs and stepped base slabs that make each pier feel anchored.

candidate_blender_tools.use: Create cap, necking, and base step slabs.
Round tiny stone edges without changing block proportions.
Keep the cap and base silhouette crisp after beveling.

components.observed_reference_shape: Small vertical accent above the cap line, simplified for v0 as a low-poly stone knob or capstone.

candidate_blender_tools.use: Create a low-vertex finial or capstone cylinder.
Soften the finial rim.

components.observed_reference_shape: Solid rectangular center panel between piers rather than open balusters.

candidate_blender_tools.use: Create the main solid guard panel block.
Plan inner face offsets before raised/recessed panel detailing.
Give the panel stone-edge highlights.

components.observed_reference_shape: Thick horizontal top coping/rail crossing between piers, visually heavier than the current prototype rail.

candidate_blender_tools.use: Create the long coping block.
Make the coping feel rounded enough to catch light.
Improve the hard-surface shading after bevels.

components.observed_reference_shape: Layered lower moldings under the center panel with narrow horizontal steps.

candidate_blender_tools.use: Create one trim strip block.
Repeat horizontal molding strips when the source declares count and offset.
Bevel strip edges so stacked moldings remain readable.

components.observed_reference_shape: Narrow repeated vertical/rectangular ornaments near the panel sides and pier edges.

candidate_blender_tools.use: Create one narrow ornament block.
Repeat ornaments along a declared local axis.
Mirror side ornament placement across the panel.
Keep small trim blocks visible after shading.

blender_tool_sequence_proposal.reason: Create simple masses, low-poly cap/finial forms, and pointed-arch cutter/trim profiles.
Cut pier recesses, repeat trim/molding, and mirror symmetric details.
Push block faces into panel/recess hierarchy and make stone edges read under lighting.
Add deterministic stone surface variation only after the forms are settled.
Generate stable UVs for procedural material review.
Separate pier, panel, trim, recess, cap, and shadow roles before preview.
Prove the generated model can be bounded, validated, previewed, and exported by the adapter.

future_reference_only_tools.use: Later hand-detail pass for emblem cracks or chipped stone, after deterministic block generation is stable.
Later texture-paint pass only if a separate authored texture workflow is created.

review_questions: Should the center infill stay solid like the reference, or become a code-like open guard with balusters?
Should pointed-arch pier recesses be shallow boolean cuts or raised trim laid over a flat pier face?
Should the top coping act as a decorative cap only, or should a later profile also model handrail-like graspability?

next_generation_goal.first_geometry_change: Replace exposed rail connector tabs with a solid panel and socket-collar composition derived from this packet.
